subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should memory-core grow a first-class multi-index config, storage, and query-routing contract for embedding failover, and what backward-compatible rollout shape should be approved?
rationale: The request is useful and aligned with reliability goals, but it changes persistent memory state, public config, provider failover semantics, and plugin-owned memory boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent API alone.

options.title: Approve Multi-Index Design
options.body: Approve a plugin-owned memory-core design covering per-model index identity, dual ingestion, active/fallback routing, status output, doctor migration, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Scalar Contract
options.body: Keep the current scalar provider/model/fallback contract and address only narrower outage or fallback-latching bugs as separate repairs.

options.title: Defer To External Plugin
options.body: Move this capability out of core only if maintainers decide an external memory plugin can implement it without missing OpenClaw APIs.

recommendation.title: Approve Multi-Index Design
recommendation.body: Approve a plugin-owned memory-core design covering per-model index identity, dual ingestion, active/fallback routing, status output, doctor migration, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current assignee and has recent memory provider availability history, making them the best available owner for the product/API decision.
